adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page hard-caps to 50 members with no pagination UI, making members beyond 50 unreachable (regression from old behavior that returned all users)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the server now always applies `limit` and `offset` with a default `limit` of 50 (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i; members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`). Previously, only *automatic* groups were limited/offset (default 200) and non-automatic groups returned the full member list. On the client side, the public group members route (`discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`) now sets the controller model to the group and calls `model.findMembers()`, and the template (`discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) iterates over `members`, but no pagination controls/actions are added for the public members page in this diff. Therefore, by default only the first 50 members are shown and there is no UI in the diff to reach subsequent pages, making members beyond 50 effectively unreachable via the normal UI (a regression from prior behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages calculation uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing an off-by-one blank page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit)
matched_golden_ids: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same off-by-one pagination bug: using Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 creates an extra blank page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and it recommends using Math.ceil instead. This matches the golden comment's underlying issue and example scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding a nonexistent username to a group silently succeeds with no error feedback, so the admin never learns the member wasn't added

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, each provided username is looked up with `User.find_by_username(username)` and only added if found. Nonexistent usernames are simply skipped with no error collection. The action then calls `group.save` and, if it returns true, responds with `success_json` regardless of whether any users were actually added. On the client, `Group#addMembers` just reloads the members list on success and does not surface any per-username failures, so an admin gets no explicit feedback that some/all usernames were invalid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the last member on the last page leaves a stale offset, causing findMembers to query beyond the new total and render an empty page

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Discourse.Group#removeMember`, after deletion it calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`. `findMembers` computes `offset` as `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`, but `user_count` is stale (still the pre-delete total) when the request is made. If you were on the last page and removed the last member (e.g., total=51, limit=50, offset=50; after delete total becomes 50), the next `findMembers` call can query with `offset=50`, which is now equal to the new total and will return an empty `members` array, leaving the UI on an empty page. The code never clamps offset to the last valid page start (e.g., `max(total - limit, 0)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Add-members input is never cleared after a successful add, leaving stale usernames displayed in the user-selector

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and contains a comment `// TODO: should clear the input`, but there is no code that resets `usernames` (e.g., `this.set("usernames", null)`) either immediately or after the AJAX request succeeds. In `Discourse.Group#addMembers`, the success handler only reloads members via `self.findMembers()` and does not clear any controller/UI state. Therefore the user-selector will keep showing the previously entered usernames after a successful add.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new GET /groups/:name/members JSON contract (members array plus meta.total/limit/offset) has no spec coverage, so meta key drift or ignored pagination params would break all member lists silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GroupsController#members` to return `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, and the frontend was updated to consume `members`/`meta`. However, the proposed finding is primarily about missing spec coverage and speculative future regressions (“meta key drift” / “ignored pagination params”), not a concrete runtime defect introduced by the diff. The absence of a test in this diff is not, by itself, a verifiable correctness bug in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The normal (non-automatic) group update path has no spec coverage after the wire format changed from nested {group: {...}} to flat {name, alias_level, visible} params, so a param-name mismatch between save() and the controller would ship silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the update wire format from nested params (previously `params[:group]` with `name`, `usernames`, etc.) to flat params (`params[:name]`, `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`) in `Admin::GroupsController#update`, and the JS model now sends `data: this.asJSON()` (flat). In the spec changes, the prior non-automatic update coverage (`context '.update'` with updating name/members and incremental patch cases) is removed and replaced with a single test that only exercises updating an *automatic* group (ensuring name is ignored). There is no remaining spec that validates the non-automatic update path accepts the new flat params and persists changes. That lack of coverage is directly observable in the diff; while an actual param mismatch is not present in the shown code, the risk of shipping such a mismatch without tests is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages helper in admin-group.js.es6 uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 which is wrong when user_count is evenly divisible by limit (e.g., 100 members with limit 50 gives 3 pages instead of 2), causing showingLast to never become true, next staying enabled, and the admin landing on a phantom empty page; should use Math.ceil and clamp to (totalPages-1) * limit

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). For counts evenly divisible by `limit` (e.g., 100 with limit 50), this yields 3 instead of 2. The `next` action sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, so on the last real page (offset 50) clicking next sets offset to 100, and `Group.findMembers` allows offset == user_count, producing an empty member list from the server. This creates a phantom empty page; `showingLast` only becomes true on that phantom page, so the UI incorrectly allows navigating past the real last page. Using `Math.ceil(user_count/limit)` (and/or clamping offset to `(totalPages-1)*limit`) would fix it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET /groups/:name/members endpoint changed from returning a bare serialized array to returning {members, meta} envelope, a breaking change to a public API contract with no back-compat that will silently break plugins, themes, or external consumers parsing the old array shape

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to return an object envelope `{ members: ..., meta: ... }` (see `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`) instead of the previous `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`, which produced a bare JSON array. The client code was updated accordingly (`group.findMembers()` now reads `result.members` and `result.meta`). This is an observable, backward-incompatible response-shape change for the public GET `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint (now `/members.json` in the client), with no compatibility layer preserving the old array format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin_base.scss restyles the Badges admin page via the new .groups, .badges selector, changing badges admin form label weight, field margins, and input widths as an undeclared side effect unrelated to group memberships

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new CSS block `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... } }`, which will apply those form styles to any admin page wrapped in `.badges`. However, this is a styling/layout change, not a verifiable functional/correctness defect. Additionally, the inclusion of `.badges` is explicit (not accidental selector bleed), and similar `.form-horizontal` styling previously existed under `section.details .form-horizontal` and was removed there—suggesting a refactor/re-scoping of existing styles rather than an unintended side effect. The finding is therefore more of a subjective “unrelated change” concern than a clear problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin_base.scss silently strips input/textarea/select { width: 350px } and bold labels from the pre-existing section.details .form-horizontal block by moving them to the new .groups, .badges selector, causing visual regressions in unrelated admin pages rendering section.details

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the shared styling from `section.details .form-horizontal` (bold `label` and `input, textarea, select { width: 350px }`, plus checkbox width) and reintroduces it only under the narrower `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... } }` selector. As a result, any admin pages that render a `.form-horizontal` inside `section.details` but are not within `.groups` or `.badges` will no longer receive those styles, changing their appearance. This is a concrete, verifiable behavioral change introduced by the diff and can cause visual regressions on unrelated admin pages using `section.details`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs and admin-group-selector.hbs contain only whitespace-only re-indentation churn, polluting blame history and inflating the apparent scope of the change

adjudication.rationale: The cited changes in `admin-group-selector.hbs` remove leading/trailing blank lines, and `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs` adjusts indentation/newlines around existing markup. These are purely formatting/blame-churn concerns and do not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect visible in the diff. As framed, it's a style/nit finding rather than a real problem per the instructions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::GroupsController#add_members reports success even when zero usernames matched — typo'd or whitespace-padded usernames are silently dropped, admin sees success, and combined with the TODO'd input clearing there is no feedback loop to tell whether an add actually happened

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code splits the provided `usernames` string and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user. If none match (e.g., typo, case/whitespace like " bob "), the loop performs zero additions, but the controller still calls `group.save` and will typically render `success_json` even though nothing changed. There is no check for “0 users added” and no error/feedback path for invalid usernames, so the proposed behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec for remove_member uses xhr :put instead of the actual delete route verb, so functional tests bypass routing and the verb/route contract for remove_member has no real coverage

The old spec asserting non-automatic group rename works via PUT :update was deleted, not migrated, leaving the live rename path (group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic) untested so future regressions in the rename branch ship undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the prior controller spec that asserted a non-automatic group could be renamed via PUT :update (it previously checked group.name == 'fred'). The new specs only cover stripping spaces on create, ignoring name changes for automatic groups, and member add/remove endpoints. However, the finding’s stronger claim that the rename branch is now untested overall is not fully verifiable from this diff alone, because other specs (not shown) could still cover renaming non-automatic groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking, unversioned API contract change on GET /groups/:name/members: response shape changed from bare JSON array to { members: [...], meta: { total, limit, offset } }, breaking existing consumers with no versioning, deprecation period, or compatibility branch

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members the response changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which returns a bare serialized collection/array) to an explicit `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. That is a concrete, breaking change in the JSON response shape for GET /groups/:group_id/members (aka /groups/:name/members). The diff updates internal JS callers/templates to use `result.members`/`meta`, but there is no compatibility branch preserving the old array shape, so any existing external consumers of that endpoint would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed membership-management API surface silently: get 'users' route deleted with no replacement or 410/redirect, PUT /admin/groups/:id no longer reads group[usernames] (silently ignores it and returns success_json), PATCH .../changes path removed, and automatic-group rejection status changed from 403 to 422
PUT /admin/groups/:id with {group: {usernames: 'a,b'}} now returns 200 success while zero membership changes occur — a silent no-op reported as success

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, the code no longer reads params[:group] or payload[:usernames]; it only updates alias_level/visible/name from top-level params, then calls group.save and returns success_json on success. Therefore a request like PUT /admin/groups/:id with body {group: {usernames: 'a,b'}} will ignore the usernames, perform no membership change, and still likely return 200 success (since saving an unchanged group typically succeeds), making it a silent no-op. Membership changes were moved to the new add_members/remove_member endpoints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: removeMember in group.js reloads via findMembers() without adjusting offset for the now-smaller member list, causing an empty page, currentPage exceeding totalPages, and both nav arrows rendering enabled
findMembers computes offset = Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0)) against the pre-response user_count and clamps to user_count rather than a page boundary, producing a misaligned partial page

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, the request offset is clamped with `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`, which allows `offset === user_count`. The controller action `next` explicitly sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, so when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), clicking next from offset 50 sets offset to 100. `findMembers` then requests `offset=100`, and the server (`GroupsController#members`) does `limit(...).offset(offset)`, returning an empty page (or a partial/misaligned page depending on count). This is a verifiable correctness bug introduced by the diff: the offset should be clamped to the last valid page boundary (e.g., `max(0, user_count - limit)` or similar), not to `user_count` itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group_member.hbs gates the remove link on {{#unless automatic}} but the item context is a Discourse.User which has no automatic property, so the remove control shows for automatic group members
removeMember and addMembers have no error handlers, so when the server rejects removal of automatic group members with 422 the failure is completely silent

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the `removeMember` and `addMembers` actions call `this.get("model").removeMember(...)` / `.addMembers(...)`, and those model methods return `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` without any `.catch`/failure callback. However, the finding’s key claim—“the failure is completely silent”—is not verifiable from this diff alone because `Discourse.ajax` may have global error handling (common in Discourse) that surfaces 422 responses automatically. The diff only shows lack of *local* error handling, not that errors are silent in the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips unresolvable usernames and never strips whitespace, then returns success_json unconditionally — e.g. ' alice' fails lookup and is skipped without feedback while the response reports success

adjudication.rationale:
In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `usernames` is taken as-is (`params.require(:usernames)`) and processed via `usernames.split(",").each` with `User.find_by_username(username)`.

This introduces two verifiable behaviors:
- Whitespace is not stripped per username, so an input like `' alice'` will not match `find_by_username` and will be skipped.
- Nonexistent/unresolvable usernames are silently ignored because of `if user = ...` with no else/error collection.

The action then returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds; it does not validate that any users were actually added, so it can report success even when all provided usernames were skipped. It’s not literally “unconditional” (it checks `group.save`), but it is success without feedback on skipped usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query pattern in add_members: usernames.split(',').each issues one User.find_by_username query per username in a loop; should use a single batched User.where(username: list)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` followed by `User.find_by_username(username)` inside the loop. That performs one DB lookup per username (N separate queries), which is a classic N+1/per-item query pattern and can be batched with a single `User.where(username: list)` (or `where(username_lower: ...)`) query.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers previously returned a promise (Ember.RSVP.resolve([])) when name was empty but now does bare return (undefined, not a promise), breaking any external caller doing group.findMembers().then(...)
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags a code path that now does a bare `return`, yielding `undefined` instead of a proper return value (previously a promise). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment: missing/implicit returns lead to `undefined` on some paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: limit and offset params on the public GET /groups/:name/members endpoint are completely unclamped — limit=100000000 loads the entire membership table in one request, and a negative offset produces an invalid SQL OFFSET error (500)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members` the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then directly applies them via `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. This means a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit`, causing the server/DB to attempt to return a very large member list in one response (potential DoS for large groups). Also, `offset` can be negative (e.g. `-1`), and ActiveRecord will pass that through to SQL `OFFSET -1`, which commonly triggers a database error (500) rather than a controlled 4xx. The finding’s “entire membership table” wording is slightly overstated (it’s the group’s membership), but the core issue (unclamped limit and potentially invalid negative offset) is real in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No request sequencing in pagination actions: next/previous fire findMembers() without disabling, aborting, or ordering in-flight requests, so the most recent response wins and can leave the header showing one page's offset/user_count while the member list shows different data
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments point to the same underlying problem: findMembers() is asynchronous and its result is not properly handled/ordered, leading to race conditions where UI/controller state can reflect out-of-order responses (e.g., member data not immediately available or mismatched with pagination/header state).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination math in admin-group.js.es6 produces a phantom empty last page when user_count is divisible by limit (totalPages off by one, offset clamped to user_count instead of user_count - limit)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In admin-group.js.es6, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is off-by-one when `user_count` is exactly divisible by `limit` (it should be `Math.ceil(...)` or equivalent). Additionally, the `next` action computes `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, allowing `offset == user_count`. `Group.findMembers` then uses that offset (clamped to `<= user_count`), and the server applies `limit(...).offset(offset)`, which yields an empty page when `offset == total` (and also skips the final partial page when `user_count` is not divisible by `limit`, because the last valid offset should be `user_count - (user_count % limit)` not `user_count`). This creates a verifiable phantom empty last page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls, a behavioral regression for groups with more than 50 members

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `GroupsController#members`, the endpoint now always applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`, regardless of group type, and returns only that slice (`members:`) plus `meta.total`. On the client, the public `group-members` route no longer sets the controller model to a full members array; it now sets `controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();`, and `Discourse.Group#findMembers` defaults to `limit: 50, offset: 0` and stores the fetched slice in `members`. The public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` was changed to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, so it will render only the first 50 fetched members. Unlike the admin group template, the public group members template/route changes add no pagination controls or actions to change `offset` and refetch. Therefore groups with >50 members will be silently truncated with no navigation in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group creation can no longer add initial members in one step; the create-with-usernames workflow and API contract (POST /admin/groups with group[usernames]) was removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the create-with-usernames flow end-to-end. On the client, `group.saveWithUsernames(this.get('usernames'))`/`createWithUsernames(...)` are replaced with `group.save()`/`group.create()`, and `Discourse.Group.asJSON()` no longer includes `usernames`. On the server, `Admin::GroupsController#create` no longer reads `params[:group][:usernames]` (or any usernames at all) and only persists `name` and `visible`. Membership changes are now split into new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints requiring an existing `group_id`. As a result, you can no longer create a group and add initial members in the same POST (and any clients still sending `group[usernames]` will no longer have members added).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale usernames in the admin group controller are never reset on model swap, so typed usernames can leak between groups and be added to the wrong group via model.addMembers

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6`, `usernames` is now just a plain property initialized to `null`, and the old computed property that derived/reset it from `members` was removed. In `admin/routes/admin_group_route.js`, `setupController` only sets `model` and calls `model.findMembers()`; it never resets `controller.usernames`. Ember route controllers are typically singletons reused across transitions, so when switching between different admin groups the same controller instance can keep the previously typed `usernames` value. The `addMembers` action uses `this.get("usernames")` directly and would therefore submit stale input to `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` for the newly selected group.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding non-existent usernames in add_members silently succeeds with a success toast and no error, and the input is never cleared so a retry re-adds everyone

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username` returns a user; missing usernames are simply skipped with no error or feedback, and the action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it will even if no users were added). On the client side, `addMembers` in `admin-group.js.es6` contains a `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not reset `this.usernames`, so the input value persists and retrying would resend the same list. The “success toast” aspect isn’t directly verifiable from this diff, but silent success + uncleared input are.

adjudication_records.issue_text: External admin API contract broken without transition: removed users route, incremental changes add/delete endpoint, and nested group[usernames] payload support cause existing clients to silently no-op or 404

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes several backwards-incompatible API changes under /admin/groups with no compatibility layer: (1) routes.rb removes the previous `get "users"` route and replaces it with `put/delete "members"`, so existing clients calling the old endpoint will 404. (2) Admin::GroupsController drops the PATCH-based incremental membership update (`update_patch` handling `params[:changes][:add]/[:delete]`); PATCH requests will still hit `update` but `params[:changes]` is ignored, so membership updates become a silent no-op. (3) `create`/`update` stop accepting nested `params[:group]` (including `group[usernames]`) and now expect top-level params, so clients using the old payload will fail to update members and potentially not set fields as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec uses xhr :put but the actual route is DELETE, so the test passes regardless of whether the DELETE route exists or is correctly wired

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the admin groups member-removal endpoint is wired as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members). But the spec shown under `context ".remove_member"` calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, which invokes the controller action directly and does not exercise the DELETE route wiring. Therefore the test would still pass even if the DELETE route were missing/miswired, so it does not verify the actual route/verb behavior introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin and group-members routes no longer wait for the findMembers promise, so transient AJAX failures render an empty member list with no spinner or error

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `afterModel` hooks in both `admin_group_route.js` and `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` that previously returned `model.findMembers()` and therefore participated in the route’s promise chain. Now `setupController` just calls `model.findMembers();` without returning/awaiting it. Since `Group#findMembers` performs `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` but the route does not consume the promise, any AJAX rejection will not trigger the route’s error handling and the UI will simply keep `members` unset/unchanged. Given the templates were changed to iterate `{{each ... in members}}`, a failed request can render an empty list with no route-level error state, which is a concrete behavioral regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded, user-controlled `limit` parameter on the public `/groups/:name/members` endpoint allows bulk user enumeration and memory/CPU exhaustion via large limit values (e.g. limit=100000000), with no maximum cap applied

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and passes it directly into `group.users...limit(limit)` with no maximum cap or validation. This makes `limit` fully user-controlled on a public endpoint (`/groups/:name/members.json` as used by `Discourse.Group#findMembers`) and allows requesting extremely large result sets, increasing DB/CPU work and response size, enabling bulk member enumeration and potential resource exhaustion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative or zero `limit`/`offset` values from request params are passed directly into ActiveRecord queries without lower-bound validation

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then uses them directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no server-side lower-bound validation/clamping, so a request can supply negative values (e.g., `limit=-1`, `offset=-10`) which ActiveRecord will pass through to SQL. This can lead to incorrect behavior (e.g., negative limit meaning “no limit” in some DBs or negative offset causing errors) and bypass intended pagination bounds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `usernames.split(",")` in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` crashes with NoMethodError (500) when `usernames` is sent as an array, since `params.require` returns an Array which has no `split` method

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. In Rails, `params[:usernames]` can validly be an Array (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` or JSON array). If an Array is provided, `split` is undefined and this will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. The diff contains no type check/coercion (e.g. `Array(usernames)` or `to_s`) before calling `split`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `params.require(:user_id).to_i` in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` crashes with NoMethodError (500) when `user_id` is sent as an array, since Array has no `to_i` method

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i`. `params.require(:user_id)` only asserts presence, not type. If a request supplies `user_id` as an array (e.g. `user_id[]=1&user_id[]=2`), Rails will produce an `Array` value for `params[:user_id]`. Ruby `Array` does not implement `to_i`, so this line will raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500. This is a real, diff-introduced robustness/correctness issue even if the normal client sends a scalar id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The primary non-automatic group update path (rename, alias_level change, visible toggle) lost all test coverage: the diff deleted the old 'is able to update group members' test and replaced the .update context with only one test covering the automatic-group edge case, so a regression in the normal-group edit flow would pass the suite green

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the previous `.update` coverage that exercised updating a normal (non-automatic) group (including setting `name` and adding members via the old update payload) and the incremental PATCH add/delete tests were removed. The new `.update` context contains only `it "ignore name change on automatic group"`, which covers only the automatic-group edge case (`id: 1`). Membership changes were moved to new endpoints (`add_members`/`remove_member`) and get their own tests, but there is no longer any test asserting the normal update flow for a regular group (e.g., renaming a non-automatic group, changing `alias_level`, toggling `visible`) works. Thus a regression in the primary non-automatic update behavior could pass the suite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The remove_member spec calls the action with the wrong HTTP verb (xhr :put instead of DELETE), so controller specs bypass routing and never verify the DELETE route wiring in routes.rb — deleting or breaking the route leaves the spec green while the admin UI remove button 404s

adjudication.rationale: In routes.rb the admin route for removing a member is wired as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` under `resources :groups`, i.e. it expects an HTTP DELETE to `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`. However, in the diff the new controller spec section for `.remove_member` begins with `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: ...`, which uses PUT instead of DELETE. Rails controller specs can invoke actions directly without going through routing, so this spec would not fail if the DELETE route is broken/removed, and it also doesn't reflect the verb used by the UI code (`type: "DELETE"` in `Group#removeMember`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'visible' assertion in the .update test cannot fail: the automatic admins group already defaults visible to true, so the assertion passes even if the 'group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"' line were deleted; no test ever sets visible to false, so the string-vs-boolean coercion logic is unverified in either direction

Both new render_json_error error branches in create and update actions have no test that triggers them — no test submits an invalid payload, so the error path and the exact JSON error shape the frontend must handle to un-set disableSave is unverified; a 500 or unparseable shape would leave the admin save button permanently disabled

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add new failure branches in Admin::GroupsController#create and #update that call render_json_error(group), and the updated spec suite shown only tests successful cases (e.g., create strips spaces; update ignores name change on automatic groups) rather than forcing validation failure. However, this is a test-coverage observation rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the code: nothing in the diff indicates render_json_error produces an unparseable/incorrect shape or causes a 500, and the claim about the frontend permanently disabling the save button depends on UI/promise error-handling not shown in the diff. So the finding is largely speculative beyond “there isn’t a test for this branch.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: The non-existent-username branch in the new add_members endpoint (username not found → silently skipped) is untested: the old spec covering this semantics was deleted without being ported, so regressions like raising 500 on unknown username or breaking on whitespace in comma-separated input would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous controller spec that explicitly asserted adding a non-existent user succeeds silently (the old “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” example under incremental PATCH update). The new implementation moves membership changes to the new `add_members` endpoint, where `usernames.split(",").each` uses `User.find_by_username(username)` and simply skips nil (the branch in question), but the updated specs add only a “add several members” success case and do not include any test for unknown usernames (or for inputs with whitespace around comma-separated usernames). So the finding that this behavior is now untested and that regressions would go undetected is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Routes for add_members/remove_member supply params[:id] but controllers require params[:group_id], so params.require(:group_id) raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and every production add/remove group member request fails
matched_golden_ids: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same root cause: routes pass the group identifier as params[:id], but the controller expects/requires params[:group_id], leading to ParameterMissing and broken add/remove (group membership) actions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Specs inject group_id directly via xhr :put instead of going through the real routes, so the route/controller param mismatch is never caught by the test suite
The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec uses xhr :put :remove_member (PUT verb) while the route only defines DELETE, so the specs never exercise the actual route/controller contract
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and candidate issue point out the same mismatch: the spec/test uses `xhr :put` (PUT) to hit `remove_member`, but the route is defined to require a DELETE method, so the test doesn’t match/exercise the real route/controller contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members endpoint response shape changed from an array to {members, meta} in one step, breaking pre-deploy clients that call result.map() with 'result.map is not a function' and removing the old array-shaped public API with no versioning or overlap window (expand+contract violation)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which returns a JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e. an object with `members` and `meta`. Previously, the client code in `Discourse.Group#findMembers` did `Discourse.ajax('/groups/' + name + '/members').then(function(result) { return result.map(...) })`, which would throw `result.map is not a function` against the new server response. The diff updates the in-repo client to the new shape, but there is no backward-compatible overlap on the public `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint, so any pre-deploy/cached clients or external consumers expecting an array will break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin groups update action silently drops the old group[usernames] payload — pre-deploy admin sessions save membership changes and get a success response while the membership change is discarded, with no dual-read of the old payload shape

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the server-side Admin::GroupsController API contract: previously `update_put` read `payload = params[:group]` and applied `payload[:usernames]` (and nested name/visible/alias_level). After the change, `update` only reads top-level `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, and `params[:name]`, and membership changes are moved to new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints. There is no backward-compatible “dual read” of `params[:group]` or `params[:group][:usernames]` (nor `params[:changes]` from the old PATCH flow). As a result, an older pre-deploy admin UI (or cached JS) that still submits `group[usernames]` (and nested fields) to `PUT/PATCH /admin/groups/:id` will get a 200 success response (group.save succeeds with no changes) while the membership update (and even name/visible/alias_level) is silently ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET /admin/groups/:id/users route removed outright with no deprecation or redirect, causing 404s for existing API consumers, and its replacement /groups/:name/members.json is not a drop-in substitution (different identifier and different auth surface)
